title: Natural Treasure Basket
strapline: Pinecones, shells, a smooth stone and a loofah — the outdoors gathered into a basket for a baby to study.
intent: Bring the textures, scents and weights of the natural world within a sitting baby's reach — bark, shell, stone, seed, sponge.
Strengthen reaching, grasping and mouthing on objects with real variety: rough and smooth, cool and light, hard and yielding.
Link the basket to the outdoors babies already notice from pram and carrier — the pinecone from the walk, the shell from home.
Support deep, unhurried exploration led entirely by the baby's own curiosity.
Lay the earliest roots of understanding the natural world, one treasure at a time.
implementation: Gather safe natural treasures: large pinecones, a big smooth stone, a chunk of bark, a whole lemon, a loofah, a large shell, a sea sponge, a wooden root — all bigger than a choke tube.
Sit the baby steadily with the basket in reach and settle low beside them, quiet and attentive.
Name softly what the baby chooses ('the pinecone — all scratchy') and hand it back when it is shown to you.
Gather fresh treasures on pram walks and invite families to bring one from home — a conker, a smooth pebble, a big seed pod.
Inspect every piece before each session for sharp points, mould or crumbling bits, wash mouthables, and retire anything that sheds.
key_questions: The pinecone is scratchy and the sponge is soft — can you feel both?
Can you smell the lemon? Your nose is working hard!
Where did we find this shell — do you remember the walk?
Which natural treasure is coming to show me?
The stone is heavy — look how you lifted it with two hands.

impact.text: Babies explore natural materials with all their senses — mouthing the shell, stroking the loofah, sniffing the lemon.
Babies reach, grasp and transfer treasures of different weights, working out heavy and light through their hands.
Connections form between the basket and the world outside — the pinecone in the basket and the tree on the pram walk.
A baby works one treasure deeply — turning the stone over, dropping it, mouthing it, studying it again.
A baby holds the shell up towards their key person and vocalises, sharing what they have found.

enhancements: A seasonal basket that changes with the walks — conkers and leaves in autumn, big smooth stones and shells in summer.
Scent added gently — a lavender bag, a cinnamon stick, a whole orange (supervised).
A natural mirror basket, so the shells and the reflection can be studied together.
Family-gathered treasures displayed with a note — 'Rowan brought this pebble from the beach'.
A soft sheepskin under the basket so the whole session is warm and grounding.

playing_exploring: The baby chooses freely from the natural treasures, exploring with no fixed outcome.
Every sense is engaged — treasures are mouthed, sniffed, stroked and stared at.
active_learning: Babies return to a favourite treasure across days, concentrating deeply when left undisturbed.
creating_thinking: Babies test what each natural thing does — does the pinecone roll, will the sponge squash? — and notice the answers.
